reason: The cited evidence (E2, E3) supports that Mo-containing BCC refractory HEAs retain high-temperature strength better than other compositions, but no evidence is provided that adding Mo to the specific TiVNbTa system preserves single-phase BCC structure, ductility, or thermal properties, nor that solid-solution strengthening from Mo alone yields the predicted 20–50% improvement without embrittlement.
premises: Mo addition to BCC refractory HEAs enhances high-temperature strength retention via solid-solution strengthening.
Mo-containing BCC refractory HEAs (e.g., MoNbTaW, MoNbTaVW) show lower reduction in yield strength at elevated temperatures compared to other MPEAs.
TiVNbTa baseline is a single-phase BCC alloy with reported yield strength ~330 MPa and compressive strength ~423 MPa at 1273 K.
Adding Mo to TiVNbTa will not compromise ductility or thermal transfer properties required for the interlayer.
